F-05.title: Durable audit writes for crisis review read operations

findings.evidence: Line 257: calls writeAuditLogEntry with caseId: null, conversationId: null, action: 'viewed', metadata includes surface: 'list_cases', filter_status, limit, offset, result_count, total. Params are mandatory (not optional). writeAuditLogEntry at line 162 is BLOCKING — throws on failure, preventing the read from returning without an audit row.

Line 554: calls writeAuditLogEntry with caseId (from params — non-null for single-case), conversationId: null, action: 'viewed', metadata includes surface: 'audit_trail_view', entries_returned. Blocking write. Reading the audit trail is itself audited — recursive correctness per SCL-025.

The cron SLA sweep is a system operation: (1) no reviewer identity — cron has no authenticated user, (2) no conversation content read — only queries crisis_review_cases for open cases past SLA deadline, (3) the sweep exists to trigger notifications, not to provide human review access. SCL-025 mandates 'every read logged' for the admin review surface — the cron sweep is not a surface read, it's an automated monitoring operation. The exemption is correct.
findings.risk_note: The optional-params shape on getBreachedCases (line 464) is a design choice, not a vulnerability. The ONLY admin caller (admin-crisis-review.ts:309) always passes params. A future caller that omits params would skip the audit row, but TypeScript's optional parameter makes this explicit, and adding a new admin route requires passing through requireSupabaseAuth + requireSupabaseAdmin middleware. Low residual risk.

findings.evidence: Line 168-169: case_id: params.caseId ?? undefined, conversation_id: params.conversationId ?? undefined. When null, Supabase client omits undefined keys from INSERT; column defaults to NULL (safe after migration 20260814000000). Functionally correct. Minor style note: explicit null would be clearer than undefined-omission, but behavior is identical.

findings.check: Admin route always passes params for SLA breaches
findings.evidence: admin-crisis-review.ts:309: getBreachedCases({ reviewerId: req.user!.id, ip: req.ip ?? ..., requestId: req.requestId }). Object literal always populated from authenticated request. No path for admin call to reach getBreachedCases without params.

findings.evidence: Test 'catches a synthetic bypass route (provability)' at line 655: writes _test-bypass-route.ts, verifies returnsTutorMessageContent returns true, verifies usesSerializer returns {imports: false, calls: false}. Cleans up in finally block. Passed in suite run (50/50).

findings.check: External planted bypass detected by structural gate
findings.evidence: Planted _audit-bypass-test.ts: from('tutor_messages').select('id, message, role'), returns data.message without serializer. Gate output: 'FAIL every route file returning tutor message content uses serializeTutorOutput — AssertionError: SERIALIZER BYPASS DETECTED — _audit-bypass-test.ts: reads tutor_messages and returns message content but does NOT import serializeTutorOutput'. File removed after test.

Layer 1: readsTutorMessages — /from("tutor_messages")/. Layer 2: selectsMessageField — /\.select\([^)]*\bmessage\b/ or select('*'). Layer 3: TUTOR_CONTENT_RETURN_PATTERNS — 5 patterns covering .message access, object literals, serialized content fields, orchestration response, last_message_preview. All three must match for a file to be flagged.
Dedicated tests: admin-crisis-review.ts (does not read tutor_messages) — not flagged. diagnostic-routes.ts (does not read tutor_messages) — not flagged. Both pass in suite.

findings.check: Snapshot delta contains only two nullability changes
findings.evidence: git diff 103a80b 485a9dc -- scripts/ci/genesis-schema.expected.sql: exactly 2 lines changed. Line 3574: 'case_id uuid NOT NULL' → 'case_id uuid'. Line 3575: 'conversation_id uuid NOT NULL' → 'conversation_id uuid'. No other changes.

Migration 20260814000000 runs ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL. This is backward-compatible: existing rows with non-null values remain valid, new rows can have NULL. No data migration needed. Table created by 20260813000000_crisis_review_queue.sql. Ordering: 20260813 < 20260814. Safe.
Lines 23-24: ROLLBACK: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN case_id SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN conversation_id SET NOT NULL. Correct reversal.

User noted production state: columns are still NOT NULL, migration NOT applied yet. The migration is a prerequisite for the writeAuditLogEntry null-case_id path. Until applied, aggregate audit writes (list cases, SLA breach, audit trail view) will fail with NOT NULL constraint violation. The code is correct FOR the post-migration state. The migration must be applied before deploying the code changes. This is the expected deployment sequence.

observations.note: writeAuditLogEntry uses params.caseId ?? undefined (null → undefined → omitted from INSERT → column defaults to NULL). Passing null directly would be more explicit. Functionally identical. Not a finding.

getBreachedCases optional-params pattern is a design choice that could allow a future caller to skip audit. Current risk is low: the only admin caller always passes params, and new admin routes require authenticated middleware. If the team prefers belt-and-suspenders, a separate function signature for cron vs admin would eliminate the optional path entirely.

Deployment ordering: migration 20260814000000 must be applied BEFORE deploying the code changes. Until the migration runs, aggregate audit writes (writeAuditLogEntry with null caseId) will fail with NOT NULL constraint violation. The writeAuditLogEntry function is BLOCKING (throws on failure), so affected admin endpoints (list cases, SLA breaches, audit trail view) will return 500 until the migration is applied. This is the expected deployment sequence.
